newsitem.title: FRANCE: French malt commitments 280,000 T since Thursday.
newsitem.headline: French malt commitments 280,000 T since Thursday.

text.p: Malting firms have drawn licences via France for 280,000 tonnes of malt exports since the European Union raised its malt export refund last Thursday, French grain officials said on Monday.
Of this total, 260,000 tonnes were taken on Friday and the rest on Monday, they said.
The EU on Thursday raised its malt export refund to 35 Ecus per tonne from a previous 32.5 Ecus.
Total licence take-up across the 15-nation EU since Thursday amount to 360,000 tonnes, industry sources estimated.
That brings the total take-up of licences since the beginning of the July/June season to 600,000 tonnes, they said. There was no immediate confirmation of the EU-wide figures.
The EU raised the malt refund in a partial response to a malt industry campaign for refunds of at least 40 Ecus per tonne to keep pace with currently strong barley export refunds.
